input.reasoning: Estimated by mapping each backlog item to effort in hours per role based on story points where given (using ~6-8 hours/point as a baseline for full-stack feature work, adjusted for complexity) and analogy-based sizing for unestimated items based on similar-sized items in the same domain. Roles engaged per task depend on the nature of the work: Backend Developer for API/service/data work, Frontend Developer for UI, QA Engineer for test design/execution (roughly 20-25% of dev effort), DevOps Engineer for infra/pipeline/observability work. Capacity check: total team FTE = 1.5 Backend + 1.0 Frontend + 0.6 QA + 0.4 DevOps = 3.5 FTE, i.e. ~140 hours/week combined at 40h/week/FTE. The backlog (24 items, several large e.g. payment integration, legacy migration, multi-currency, RBAC) realistically represents 4-5 months of delivery at this staffing level, so hours were allocated accordingly per role and checked against reasonable multi-month elapsed capacity (Backend ~1.5 FTE x ~18 weeks ≈ 1080h, Frontend ~1.0 FTE x18 weeks ≈720h, QA 0.6x18≈432h, DevOps 0.4x18≈288h) to avoid overloading thinly-staffed roles like DevOps and QA. Non-labour costs include Stripe integration sandbox/PCI review, cloud infra for staging/migration, and a legacy Oracle data migration tooling/consultancy allowance. Priority breakdown sums task-level estimated cost by priority bucket. Reductions identify concrete descope/defer opportunities (Low priority items, deferring legacy decommission, deferring multi-currency, trimming migration scope with phased approach) with dollar savings computed from the hours removed at blended role rates.

nonLabourLines.description: Stripe integration setup, PCI-related review and sandbox/webhook testing tooling
Legacy Oracle data migration tooling / one-off DB extraction & validation consultancy
Cloud infrastructure (staging, CI runners, observability stack) for project duration
Translation/localization and FX rate data feed subscription (multi-currency)
Accessibility audit by external WCAG 2.2 AA specialist

assumptions: No historical actuals (real spend data) are available for this project; estimate is based purely on backlog description, story points where given, and analogy-based sizing for unestimated items.
1 story point ≈ 6-7 hours of combined effort as a rough calibration anchor, adjusted per task complexity and cross-role split.

Unestimated items were sized by analogy to similarly-scoped items in the backlog with known points (e.g. PW-2 component library ~ sized similarly to PW-5 dashboard; PW-8 legacy migration sized larger due to explicit data volumes).

QA Engineer effort is assumed at roughly 25-30% of combined dev (Backend+Frontend) hours per task, reflecting a 0.6 FTE capacity constraint; QA is thinly staffed relative to backlog size and will likely be a throughput bottleneck if all items are pursued in parallel.

DevOps Engineer (0.4 FTE) hours are concentrated on CI/staging setup (PW-1), migration support (PW-8), rate limiting (PW-21) and observability (PW-22); this role is also thinly staffed and may gate delivery of infra-heavy items.
Backend Developer at 1.5 FTE is the primary bottleneck-resolving role and carries the largest hour allocation given the API, integration, and data-heavy nature of most tasks.
Elapsed project duration assumed at approximately 16-20 calendar weeks running most roles near full utilization of their FTE capacity.
Legacy data migration (PW-8) and multi-currency (PW-14) are assumed to require external tooling/consultancy beyond pure labour hours, captured as non-labour costs.
A 10% contingency buffer is applied to cover estimation uncertainty typical of a backlog with several unestimated items.

Priority breakdown totals are approximate allocations of labour+non-labour cost by the task's stated priority bucket, excluding the generic contingency line which is not attributed to a specific priority (attributed to Low here as residual placeholder for arithmetic completeness).

reductions.description: Descope Low-priority items not essential for MVP launch: PW-12 (support ticket submission), PW-18 (admin back-office), PW-19 (usage analytics), PW-23 (contract tests), PW-24 (legacy decommission) — defer to a phase 2 backlog.
reductions.effect: Removes an estimated ~340 combined hours across Backend/Frontend/QA/DevOps roles tied to these five Low-priority tickets.

reductions.description: Defer Multi-currency support (PW-14) until post-launch; ship with USD-only initially.
reductions.effect: Removes FX integration, settlement logic, and associated QA/localization non-labour cost.

reductions.description: Phase the legacy data migration (PW-8): migrate customer records first, defer bulk invoice-line historical migration to a background job post-launch.
reductions.effect: Reduces upfront Backend hours and external migration tooling/consultancy spend by roughly 40%.

reductions.description: Reduce QA Engineer allocation on lower-risk UI-only tasks (e.g. PW-2 design system, PW-20 responsive layout) by relying more on automated visual regression tooling instead of manual QA passes.
reductions.effect: Cuts ~80 QA hours from lower-risk tasks while retaining full QA coverage on payment, auth and security-critical paths.

reductions.description: Drop the external accessibility specialist audit and instead have the in-house team self-certify against WCAG 2.2 AA using automated tooling (axe, Lighthouse) supplemented by a lighter manual spot-check.
reductions.effect: Removes the external audit non-labour line item entirely.
